title: "Does elevation affect baseball hitting?"
format: html
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(Lahman)
```

The article [*Effects of altitude and atmospheric conditions on the flight of a
baseball*](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/228668381_Effects_of_altitude_and_atmospheric_conditions_on_the_flight_of_a_baseball)
motivates this question. The plot below uses Lahman's player batting data from
2010-2025 and stadium elevations to compare each hitter-season with the elevation
of the ballpark in which it was played.

```{r}
#| label: elevation-and-hitting
#| fig-cap: "Hitter-season home run rates by ballpark elevation, 2010-2025."
#| warning: false
 
park_elevations <- tribble(
  ~teamID, ~elevation_feet,
  "ARI", 1086, "ATL", 1050, "BAL", 20, "BOS", 20,
  "CHN", 596, "CHA", 594, "CIN", 482, "CLE", 653,
  "COL", 5180, "DET", 600, "HOU", 50, "KCA", 910,
  "LAA", 160, "LAN", 267, "FLA", 7, "FLO", 7, "MIA", 7, "MIL", 593,
  "MIN", 840, "NYN", 12, "NYA", 55, "OAK", 25,
  "PHI", 40, "PIT", 743, "SDN", 13, "SFN", 13,
  "SEA", 30, "SLN", 450, "TBA", 42, "TEX", 600,
  "TOR", 250, "WAS", 25, "ATH", 25
)

Batting |>
  filter(yearID >= 2010) |>
  mutate(plate_appearances = AB + BB + coalesce(HBP, 0) + coalesce(SF, 0)) |>
  filter(plate_appearances >= 50) |>
  inner_join(park_elevations, by = "teamID") |>
  mutate(home_runs_per_100_pa = 100 * HR / plate_appearances) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = elevation_feet, y = home_runs_per_100_pa)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.18, size = 1, color = "#2c7fb8") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, color = "#d95f02") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Home run rates rise with ballpark elevation",
    x = "Approximate stadium elevation (feet)",
    y = "Home runs per 100 plate appearances"
  )
```
